description:
FOUND s499e (Opus, 2026-09-27) while shipping #2380 (possessive quantifiers).

perl 5.40.3 vs PCL (tree after #2380):
    print eval { "aab" =~ /^a ++b/x ? 1 : 0 } // "died", "\n";   # perl 1, PCL died
    my $p = "^a+ +b"; print eval { "aab" =~ /$p/x ? 1 : 0 } // "died", "\n";  # perl 1, PCL died

CAUSE: perl-regex-to-ppcre receives the pattern WITHOUT its modifiers, and the one rewrite scan (%pcl-rewrite-scan) reads the space as a literal atom, so `a ++` becomes `a(?> +)`, which cl-ppcre's extended mode then reads as `a(?>+)` and refuses.  Before #2380 the same pattern also died (cl-ppcre: "Quantifier '+' not allowed"), so this is NOT a regression -- it is the /x residue of #2380.

FIX SHAPE: the scan needs to know /x (and inline (?x) / (?-x) scopes): under /x, unescaped whitespace and `#` comments are not atoms and are skipped when looking for the atom a quantifier applies to.  Either thread the modifiers into perl-regex-to-ppcre (four call sites) or move the possessive arm after %pcl-normalize-extended.  Also a `#` comment under /x that contains `(` could desynchronise the scan's group stack (no case seen).

=== DONE (s499k) ===
Shape: thread the modifiers (not "move the possessive arm after normalize" -- %pcl-normalize-extended runs only in %pcl-build-scanner and only for self-x patterns).  perl-regex-to-ppcre takes &optional EXTENDED; the four call sites pass /x (%p-regex-parts, %p-regex-op, %p-qr-parts, the s/// compile).  The scan struct gains an x slot + a per-group xstack; %pcl-rx-scan-open-group reads flag headers through the existing %pcl-parse-x-flag-group (flag-only `(?x)` sets the enclosing scope and is no atom; `(?x:`/`(?-x:`/`(?^…:` push); under /x a blank or `#…<NL>` comment is copied and is NOT the atom, and the possessive test skips blanks/comments before the `+` (%pcl-rx-insignificant-end).  The `#` desync risk the task named is closed too (a comment is copied whole).  The pre-test %pcl-has-possessive knows /x (and inline x via %pcl-has-x-modifier).  The `(?^` removal and the charset strip moved AFTER the scan so the scan sees the caret.  %pcl-rx-x-blank-p is the one /x blank set (normalize-extended uses it too).
Probes = perl: /a ++b/x, /a+ +b/x, /a + +b/x, comment (incl. `(`/`[` inside) between, (?x)a ++, (?x: a ++ ), (?x:a) ++, /xx, x-possessive gives nothing back; breaking cases (?-x:a ++) under /x, [ ]++ and \ ++ under /x, no-x `a ++`/`a+ +` unchanged.  Not this task: `(?^:a ++)` inside a /x pattern still dies -- the caret reset is dropped at the cl-ppcre layer (filed #2500).
Guard: Pl/t/regexp-subst-01.t row 53 (FAILS on 937e7b65).  ir-spec §10-poss.
subject: under /x a possessive quantifier with WHITESPACE before it (`/a ++b/x`, `/a+ +b/x`) still DIES in PCL; perl reads it as `a++` -- the #2380 rewrite scan does not know /x, so the space is read as the quantified atom
